summary: Combine result rows while keeping repeated occurrences.
documentation: UNION ALL concatenates rows from compatible SELECT statements without removing duplicates. Each side needs the same number of output columns. A final ORDER BY controls the combined result rather than either source table alone.
inputs: Two or more SELECT results with matching column counts.
returns: One combined result set retaining all source occurrences.
caution: UNION removes duplicate rows, while UNION ALL preserves them. Never assume table or branch order is the report’s display order.
scenarios: Combine two sales channels while preserving separate purchases.
Merge current and archived logs for one report.
Collect counts from multiple event sign-in sources.
title: Combine channel sales
problem: Tables shop_sales(cents INTEGER) and market_sales(cents INTEGER) each contain non-NULL sales. Return one cents column containing every sale from both tables, duplicates included, ordered by cents ascending.
goal: Use UNION ALL or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Combine with UNION ALL and add a final ORDER BY.
starter:
